claims: Finding 1: `CODERABBIT_REVIEW_RUN_MARKER = /\*\*Run ID\*\*:\s*`[^`\r\n]+`/i` (scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:4) hangs the `reviewed` state on an unverified external format contract — if the marker is absent or moves, `codeRabbitReviewSignal` can never reach `reviewed`, so every PR closeout posts one extra `@coderabbitai review` and net ladder spend goes up while the projection reports success
ADR 0066 records no dated "checked on" evidence line for the review-body format (unlike every other external claim), and the commit message is a bare subject line
No test can catch the `**Run ID**` marker contract: every test hand-writes the body (`pr-ready-state.test.mjs:2227,2274`)

Finding 2: `isCodeRabbitFinalHeadReviewRequestBody(body)` (scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:774) requires both `@coderabbitai review` and the generated marker, so a human's bare `@coderabbitai review` is invisible (returns `stale`) and the babysit closeout posts a duplicate `@coderabbitai review` for the same head

Finding 3: the canonical runbook and the skills that defer to it give opposite orderings — `docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md:399-409` makes closeout step 8 after the ready-state check, while `.claude/skills/babysit-pr/SKILL.md:295`, `.agents/…/SKILL.md:295`, `docs/notes/pr-operating-card.md:157` and `.claude/skills/ship/SKILL.md:214-216` say apply it before the final projection pair; two agents on the same PR post the request at different points, and the `pr-ready-state.md` order permits all-clear at step 10 without re-running feedback-state after the request

Finding 4: no author check on the request comment loop (scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:772-784) unlike the review loop's `CODERABBIT_AUTHORS` check at 761 — any comment from any account carrying the marker with the current head sets `requested` and suppresses the closeout (confirmed: a comment from `random-drive-by` returns `requested`)

Finding 5: sample JSON in the owning doc is stale — `docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md:276-297` (gates block) and `:305` (top-level `codexReviewSignal`) omit `codeRabbitReviewSignal` although the field is now unconditionally present

Finding 6: `scripts/coderabbit-config.test.mjs:124` lost its invariant — `assert.equal(…, 5)` is redundant with the `deepEqual` pin at line 61 and encodes nothing, so for this key the file is no longer the negative control its header claims

The 2→5 raise increases spend on both axes (more auto-reviews per PR plus a new manual closeout request), and the capacity numbers at ADR 0066:214-215 (4/hour, degradation past 90/week) were not recomputed against the 29-PR sample

The closeout isn't a wait point — `docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md:116-118` and step 9's optional-lag stance permit all-clear before the requested review returns, so on a fast PR the request buys nothing but spend
Latent pre-existing: `isCurrentReviewSignal` (658) compares review commit OIDs case-sensitively while the new marker path lowercases — an uppercase review OID yields `stale`

judge_reasoning.3829654081: The review never discusses file length, the 600-line cap, or splitting pr-ready-state-core.mjs; its scope note counts diff lines only.
judge_reasoning.3829659544: Finding 5 states the sample JSON gates block at docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md omits codeRabbitReviewSignal though the field is documented and always emitted — same defect.
judge_reasoning.3829659546: Finding 3 documents the contradictory ordering between pr-ready-state.md step 8 and the ship/babysit skills plus operating card, and recommends one canonical sequence — same defect.
judge_reasoning.3829659550: The review's classifier findings concern a bare human request lacking the marker (finding 2) and a missing author check on the comment loop (finding 4); it never raises the currentHeadOid === null fallback to review timestamps / unconditional marked-request acceptance.

1.why: Regex at pr-ready-state-core.mjs:4 exists as quoted, but the claim is a hedged 'if the external format is absent or moves' fragility argument; I cannot verify CodeRabbit's real review-body format offline, and the gate is optional (required:false), so no demonstrated defect.

2.why: True that ADR 0066's Evidence section (lines 263-300) has dated lines only for pricing/pause-sample and none for the `**Run ID**` body format, and `git log -1` is a bare subject — but this is a documentation/commit-convention note naming no concrete failure.

3.why: Tests do hand-write the body (pr-ready-state.test.mjs:2229, 2274), but that is inherent to unit-testing an external format; it names no defect beyond claim 1's speculation.

4.why: isCodeRabbitFinalHeadReviewRequestBody (core.mjs:774-441) requires the HTML marker, so a human's bare `@coderabbitai review` is skipped by the loop (state stays missing, not 'stale' as claimed) and the documented closeout then posts a second request — unlike classifyCodexReviewSignal, which accepts a bare `@codex review` bound by timestamp.

5.why: Restates the pr-ready-state.md step-8/step-10 ordering defect already listed as known at docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md:408 (Functional Correctness, Major); confirmed skills say 'before the final pair' while the runbook places it after step 7 and allows all-clear at 407-408.

6.why: The unauthenticated request-comment loop (core.mjs:772-784, no CODERABBIT_AUTHORS check unlike line 761) is the known 'Trust only authorized closeout requests' / 'Authenticate closeout markers' item (core.mjs:783, review-signals.mjs:226, cloud-watch-loop.md:53).

7.why: Confirmed the sample JSON gates block (pr-ready-state.md:276-297) and top-level line 305 omit codeRabbitReviewSignal though summarizeReadyState always emits it — this is the known Data Integrity & Integration / Minor item in that file.

8.why: coderabbit-config.test.mjs:124 does tautologically assert EXPECTED_CONFIG's own line-61 value, but the exact-equality pin and the negative-control test (105-119) are unchanged and still catch any config weakening, so the claimed loss of protection is a style/redundancy note, not a defect.

9.why: ADR 0066:213-221 does keep the 4/hour and 90/week numbers unchanged, but 'not recomputed against the 29-PR sample' asserts no concrete error or breached limit — a request for more analysis.

10.why: Accurate description of intent (lines 123-128 keep CodeRabbit advisory and rerun feedback-state only if the review lands while watching, per ADR 0066), so this is disagreement with a deliberate advisory design, not a defect.

11.why: isCurrentReviewSignal:658-659 does compare OIDs with `===` while the new marker path lowercases, but it is pre-existing (also used by the Codex path) and GitHub returns lowercase OIDs, so no realistic failure is demonstrated.
